name: Notburga-Museum Eben am Achensee
kurzbeschreibung: The Notburga-Museum in Eben am Achensee: the only museum honouring Tyrol's most beloved folk saint, Notburga von Rattenberg, housed in a Baroque vicarage since 2004.
beschreibung:
Overview

The steeped-in-tradition Notburga-Museum is situated in the idyllic pilgrimage village of Eben am Achensee at the entrance to the Achensee valley in Tyrol's Schwaz district. Housed in the heritage-listed premises of the historic vicarage directly adjacent to the magnificent Baroque pilgrimage church of St. Notburga, this establishment is the only museum in Austria dedicated exclusively to the most famous and cherished female folk saint of the Alpine region: Saint Notburga von Rattenberg (approx. 1265?1313). Opened in 2004 and honoured with the prestigious Tyrolean Museum Prize, this specialist museum provides profound insights into medieval piety, Tyrolean social history, and the vibrant folk religious devotion of past centuries.

Saint's Legend & Museum Treasures

In the 13th century, Notburga lived as a humble maidservant at Rottenburg Castle in Buch near Jenbach and later on a farmstead in Eben. Throughout her life, she selflessly devoted herself to assisting the poor, the sick, and female domestic servants. The legend of the Sickle Miracle achieved worldwide fame: when her employer attempted to force her to continue harvesting on the eve of the Sabbath, Notburga threw her sickle into the sky, where it remained suspended freely in mid-air as a sign confirming divine rest on the holy day. Following her death in 1313, tradition relates that her body was drawn on a driverless cart pulled by two oxen directly to the chapel in Eben. Inside the museum, over 200 valuable original artefacts across several storeys document the veneration of the patron saint of farmers, domestic servants, and the poor. On display are ornate Baroque processional figures, gold-woven votive gifts, historical charters, handwritten prayer books, and masterworks of Baroque sacred art by painters such as Franz Anton Zeiller. An interactive tour illuminates the demanding everyday work and life of the rural Tyrolean population in the High and Late Middle Ages. Directly neighbouring the museum, the Baroque Wallfahrtskirche St. Notburga houses the saint's relics: a globally unique feature is the Baroque high tomb, in which the saint's skeleton rests standing upright inside a glass shrine above the high altar.

Visit & Getting There

The Notburga-Museum is open from early May until late October: Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (closed on Mondays). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. ?6.00, seniors and groups approx. ?5.00, children and youth up to 18 years enjoy free admission! With the regional Achensee Erlebniscard, admission is free. Visits to the adjoining pilgrimage church are freely accessible daily and free of charge. Travel by public transport: ?BB trains to Jenbach station, from where the historic Achenseebahn (steam cog railway) or bus route 4080 runs directly to the stop Maurach/Eben Kirche (approx. two minutes' walk). By car: Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wiesing/Achensee), continuing along the Achenseestra?e B181 for about five kilometres up to Eben; free parking spaces are available directly by the vicarage.

Tips

Access to the museum on the ground floor and the forecourt of the pilgrimage church is barrier-free; assistance is available for accessing the upper exhibition rooms in the historic vicarage. Be sure to allow sufficient time to explore the church interior featuring splendid Rococo ceiling frescoes. The traditional Notburgatag on 13 September draws thousands of celebratory visitors every year with a magnificent traditional costume procession.
